items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: So he fire the single trumpet player, Mouse Randolph from St.

ctx.x: So he said, you know, that guy you sent ain't bad. I say, the guy's terrific. That's a hell (inaudible). I said, I want you -- want to hear that from you. That guy is something else. You haven't heard anything yet.

Two, three weeks after he come and he say, let's get hold of that guy. So he fire the single trumpet player, Mouse Randolph from St. Louis. He fire him, took on Dizzy in the band. So I say, now, the best thing for you to do to develop what you're doing, you got to get hold of that piano player and the bass player, and you corner. Tell ahead of time what you want them to do harmonically. You know why? Because you play a whole lot of changes they don't use in this band.
So he did that, and the guys -- especially Hinton went crazy about the guy. So he started to develop, develop.
